h1: CodeNest Coding Platform — Education & Community Hero Section Design
tagline: Hero section reference built on black #000000 and green #5ED29C, set in Instrument Serif and measured against 50px spacing steps.
summary: Hero section reference for an education or community brand — Instrument Serif, #000000 base, a 800x576 frame and React and Tailwind CSS.
about: CodeNest Coding Platform was captured at 800x576 and kept as a specification rather than as a gallery image. The colour scheme is black #000000 underneath and green #5ED29C carrying the accents, and the page is set in Instrument Serif. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 800x576 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. It is the right reference for an education or community brand hero section that has to look deliberate on the first screen.

layout.title: The bar shares the page grid
layout.body: The bar is the quietest part of the composition: wordmark, a short row of links and one #5ED29C action, all held at the smallest type step in the brief. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #5ED29C action is the only element in the bar with any weight. Test the bar over your own media before giving it a background.

layout.title: Nothing here is inherited
layout.body: Sizes were read off the render at 800x576: 50px spacing steps. A rebuild that hits those numbers looks like the reference without further tuning.

layout.title: One idea per panel
layout.body: Where a run of copy would go, this page puts a set of panels, which is what keeps the hero section scannable. Every panel uses the same internal arrangement, so the grid can be scanned by shape.

layout.title: A navigation bar that gets out of the way
layout.body: The bar sits over the 800x576 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

motion.title: The controls are the interactive layer
motion.body: Feedback is limited to hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, which is what keeps a dense first screen from feeling busy. Feedback is limited to the controls, so the composition stays still around them.

motion.title: Motion that stays out of the way
motion.body: The brief leaves animation out and lets the 800x576 layout carry the page, with hover and press states the only changes. The composition holds still, so the hierarchy has to carry the page and it does. Keep motion to the controls.

editorial.title: Why the education brief holds
editorial.body: The reason this works for an education or community brand is that it never asks the reader to assemble the message. Layout, type and colour are decided (black #000000 and green #5ED29C, set in Instrument Serif), so the first screen reads as a finished argument rather than a pile of parts. CodeNest Coding Platform states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: The order behind the hero section
editorial.body: If your page currently leads with features, this is the order to copy: navigation, the headline, the stats row, the card grid and the background clip in front, the supporting detail after, and 50px spacing steps setting the distance. A education reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: How the hero section reflows
editorial.body: Responsive here means the scale changes and the sequence does not. the navigation collapses into a mobile menu, and the reading order stays where the brief put it. The narrow layout is a decision rather than a squeeze, and the hierarchy survives it.

faq.question: How long is the prompt behind CodeNest Coding Platform?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 800x576, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: How much of CodeNest Coding Platform depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: CodeNest Coding Platform was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How should I handle the CodeNest Coding Platform media in a client build?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 800x576.
